frozen_original.title: Trump Signs EO Allowing Surveillance of US Citizens Without FISA Warrants
frozen_original.synopsis: In March 2025, the Trump administration signed a proposed executive order and issued internal guidance asserting expanded presidential authority to conduct surveillance of US citizens without obtaining Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act warrants, claiming the president's commander-in-chief authority superseded FISA requirements. The move echoed the warrantless surveillance program revealed by Edward Snowden and was immediately challenged as a violation of the Fourth Amendment. FISA court judges issued sealed orders questioning the administration's legal authority. Civil liberties organizations filed legal challenges arguing the order was a direct assault on Fourth Amendment protections against unreasonable government surveillance.

frozen_original.title: Trump Claims 'Absolute Immunity' for Any Presidential Action
frozen_original.synopsis: Trump and his legal team formally asserted in April 2025 that the Supreme Court's July 2024 immunity ruling in Trump v. United States granted him absolute immunity from accountability for essentially any action taken in office, including actions clearly outside core executive functions. The expansive interpretation went far beyond what even the conservative Supreme Court majority had written, claiming that virtually any presidential act could be characterized as official and thus immune from criminal or civil accountability. Constitutional scholars described the claim as incompatible with the rule of law and the principle that no person is above the law. The claim was being tested in multiple ongoing criminal and civil proceedings against Trump.
